findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the chemical dish machine was not sanitizing at an effective concentration of Chlorine (10ppm). CORRECTED: PIC determined that the sanitizer dispenser was empty and replaced the dispenser with a new bucket during the inspection. Chemical dish machine was then measured to be sanitizing at effective concentration of Chlorine for warewashing (50ppm). Ensure that chemical sanitizers used in mechanical warewashing are used per manufacturer’s instructions regarding pH.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed the front dress prep cooler was not sufficiently cooling and cold holding TCS foods (see Violation #33):

(i) sliced tomatoes (probed 52°F) and shredded lettuce (47°F). CORRECTED: tomatoes and lettuce were voluntarily discarded, as they were prepared longer than 4 hours ago; previously prepped tomatoes and lettuce were taken from the walk-in cooler and placed in ice baths, which will be monitored for cold holding temperatures.

(ii) shredded cheese (52°F) and cooked spaghetti (56°F). CORRECTED: shredded cheese and cooked spaghetti were voluntarily discarded, as they were removed from proper cold holding temperatures longer than 4 hours ago; a new container of shredded cheese was prepared and new packages of cook spaghetti were moved from the walk-in cooler and both were kept in a nearby short cooler that was sufficiently cold holding.

(iii) milk (42°F) and manufactured sauces that require refrigeration (clucked sauce, mayonnaise, and garlic spread - 43°F). CORRECTED: sauces were moved to nearby coolers that were sufficiently cold holding.

Ensure that TCS foods are kept at temperatures of 41°F or less.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Observed the front dress prep cooler was not sufficiently cooling and cold holding TCS foods. PIC took care of TCS foods so that they will be properly cold holding in the interim (see Violation #22). PIC is contacting a repair company. Inspector will Follow Up with establishment to confirm that the prep cooler has been repaired. Ensure that equipment for cooling and cold holding is sufficient to provide food temperatures of 41°F or less.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment:
Observed that the following freezers had significant ice drip buildup that was falling onto food:
(i) the walk-in freezer. Staff had placed a pan to collect drips, but additional ice drips had formed missing the pan and falling onto food. CORRECTED: PIC moved food away from the fans where the ice is forming and dripping.
(ii) the 2-door standing freezer. CORRECTED: PIC placed a tray directly underneath where the ice drips are forming so that when they defrost they do not fall below onto the food.
Ensure that freezers do not get significant ice buildup, and that the ice does not contaminated the food stored in the freezers.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed there is an accumulation of grease and food reside underneath the burger grills. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of grease deposits and other soil accumulations. Ensure that underneath the burger grills is clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed the ice scoop at the drive through was stored with the handle in contact with the ice. Since the handle is touched by bare hands storing the scoop in this position poses the risk of contamination. The PIC and employee working the drive through were educated and the ice scoop was moved to another location. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are always stored to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned:

(1) The food debris inside both of the microwaves on the prep line.

(2) The food debris on the shelf below the sauces on the prep line. 

(3) The dust on the hood system that is not in use anymore near the drive through and fryers. 

The above referenced were cleaned to sight and touch during the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The inspector educated the employee when the action was observed. Immediately afterwards the employee re-washed their hands using the proper procedure. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed that the following non-food contact surfaces required cleaning to protect food from cross contamination: (1) Inside the microwave located between the fryers and vegetable prep cooler; and (2) The fan blades in the walk-in cooler. The PIC cleaned both of these surfaces during the inspection. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination during storage and preparation. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Observed knives and forks stored in a container adjacent to the vegetable prep cooler with handles and food-contact surfaces intermingled. Utensils must be stored with the food contact surfaces facing in the same direction to ensure only handles are touched by employees. The PIC removed the utensils, washed them in the dish machine, and stored the clean utensils in the correct storage order. Ensure that utensils are always stored correctly to protect them from contamination. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.
